title: Lights Out
paragraphs: One of radio's landmark horror anthologies, using sound and surreal situations to explore ghosts, monsters, murder, the supernatural, and psychological terror in stories associated especially with Wyllis Cooper and Arch Oboler.

Landmark horror anthology created by Wyllis Cooper and later led by Arch Oboler. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 159 objects, including 67 exact same-date duplicate pairs and one undated archive object. Three later-dated GRH audio pairs contain earlier recordings despite metadata for distinct later broadcasts.

GRH documents the program through Wyllis Cooper national NBC era (April 18, 1935 to June 3, 1936) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Arch Oboler NBC era (June 10, 1936 to August 16, 1939) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], CBS sponsored revival (October 6, 1942 to September 28, 1943) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and NBC summer revival (1945-07 to 1945-09) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Arch Oboler (host on 37 recordings, writer on 37 recordings, director on 3 recordings, and producer on 3 recordings), Frank Martin (commercial spokesman on 13 recordings and announcer on 8 recordings), Mercedes McCambridge (performer on 8 recordings), Albert Crews (director on 5 recordings and producer on 5 recordings), Wyllis Cooper (writer on 5 recordings and director on 1 recording), Boris Aplon (performer on 4 recordings), and Lou Merrill (performer on 4 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include death, burial and confinement, murder and violent death, monsters and inhuman creatures, curses, occult forces and ritual, dangerous science and experiments, and ghosts and hauntings.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Experimental radio horror and sound design, Wyllis Cooper to Arch Oboler creative transition, 1942-43 CBS revival and script reproduction, and Lights Out as a cross-media horror property.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (21 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (18 shared credited people), [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (18 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (19 shared credited people), and [[show|richard-diamond-private-detective|Richard Diamond, Private Detective]] (16 shared credited people).
